schema:
CREATE TABLE "EMPLOYEES" ("emp_id" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, "emp_name" TEXT);
CREATE TABLE "SALARIES" ("emp_id" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, "amount" REAL, FOREIGN KEY ("emp_id") REFERENCES "EMPLOYEES" ("emp_id"));
correct_query: SELECT emp_id, emp_name FROM (SELECT LHS.emp_id AS emp_id, LHS.amount AS amount, LHS.emp_name AS emp_name, LHS.max_amount AS max_amount, RHS.emp_id AS emp_id_other, RHS.amount AS amount_other FROM (SELECT emp_id, amount, emp_name, MAX(amount) OVER () AS max_amount FROM (SELECT LHS.emp_id AS emp_id, LHS.amount AS amount, RHS.emp_name AS emp_name FROM salaries AS LHS INNER JOIN employees AS RHS ON (LHS.emp_id = RHS.emp_id))) AS LHS CROSS JOIN salaries AS RHS) WHERE (amount = amount_other AND max_amount <> amount_other) ORDER BY emp_id, emp_name NULLS LAST

expected_semantic_errors_to_be_caught.description: Mutant replaces the self-join on non-unique attribute amount (amount = amount_other AND max_amount <> amount_other) with a single-table scalar subquery inequality filter, failing to preserve join multiplicity when multiple rows share the same non-maximum amount.
expected_semantic_errors_to_be_caught.query: SELECT T1.emp_id, T1.emp_name FROM employees AS T1 JOIN salaries AS T2 ON T1.emp_id = T2.emp_id WHERE T2.amount < (SELECT MAX(amount) FROM salaries)
